summary:
PayBox is MoonPay's agent wallet and credential vault. It launched publicly on July 29, 2026 for Claude and ChatGPT through a custom MCP connector, reached grok.com on Aug 31, and added CLI support for computer-based agents: Grok Bot and Grok Computer in SDK 0.8.5 (Aug 31), and Meta's Muse in SDK 1.0.0 (Sept 17). It is run by Launchpad Limited, a BVI company that MoonPay describes as an unregulated group entity. Launchpad is also the hackathon sponsor. The public voices are CEO Ivan Soto-Wright, quoted at every launch, and Neeraj Prasad, Chief Engineer at MoonPay Labs and an ex-Dawn Labs founder. The first SDK release was published from a dawnlabs.ai npm account. The security pitch rests on Sodot (MPC and TEE), which MoonPay bought in April 2026. MoonX is not a partner. Its npm packages are maintained by MoonPay and describe a Privy-like embedded-wallet platform with passkey-protected MPC signing.

The plugin catalog:
- **World** is World Prediction Markets, a Solana protocol run by an anonymous team. It routes orders to Solana liquidity providers, issues SPL outcome tokens, resolves markets with Chainlink and settles in Phantom's CASH stablecoin. It replaced Kalshi/DFlow inside Phantom from June 1, 2026.
- In PayBox, World's money tools are geofenced and MCP-only. World and Hyperliquid tools existed before launch (SDK 0.7.0, July 8).
- MoonPay announced three more first-party additions: Kamino on Aug 27 (its "first lending and yield plugin", blocked in the US, UK, EU and Australia), Jupiter on Sept 3 (limit orders, DCA, earn) and Sunrise in September.
- The public app bundle's plugin logo map also lists xp, collector-crypt, aave, whop and maple, plus a dflow icon. The approval screens already handle ticket_purchase (seats, paid in USDC on Solana), commerce_purchase and prediction_trade. This strongly suggests ticketing, collectibles, digital goods and more yield venues are live or close.
- The x402 launch merchants (AgentRes/Resy, Purch/Amazon, BRIJ flights) are found through discover_services, not the plugin catalog.

There are two plugin types:
- **Official plugins** are enabled from the app. Discovery returns a contract_uri of the form paybox://plugins/<slug>, plus an enable_url when the plugin is off.
- **Unofficial plugins** are served by an /api/open-plugins API with two kinds:
  - **Remote:** an MCP server connected by URL, with optional OAuth. Its x402 calls go to its "connected origin".
  - **Sandbox:** a versioned bundle hosted by PayBox. Before enabling it, the user reviews its network hosts, developer-provided credentials, environment settings and tools.
- Hackathon entries are sandbox plugins. Each version needs manual approval before publication, and the marketplace has not opened to the public yet.

The hackathon runs Oct 16, 8am to Oct 17, 8pm EDT, in person (reportedly at MoonPay's NYC office) and online. @PayBox announced it at about 13:50 UTC on Oct 16. No judges, Discord, Telegram or office hours are published. Submission may require MoonPay KYC under the same email as the PayBox account.

On distribution, Cursor's marketplace approved the PayBox plugin. The pull request adding PayBox to xAI's plugin marketplace (#413) is still open. I found no formal partnership statement from xAI, Anthropic or OpenAI.

Gaps (my inference): the catalog has no creative or generative tools and no merchant-side tools such as invoicing, Solana Pay or MoonPay Commerce. Prediction markets go little beyond World. The homepage promises (yield "compared and executed", gas top-ups, rebalancing, pay-per-use research) are only partly covered. I could not finish checking what other participants are building because the shared web-search budget ran out.

key_facts.fact: PayBox officially launched July 29, 2026 as a payment vault for Claude and ChatGPT via a custom connector. Launch chains: Solana, Ethereum, Hyperliquid, Tempo, Base, Robinhood Chain, Arbitrum, Polygon. It names Visa's agentic commerce protocol, x402 and Sodot MPC. Coming soon: more AI platforms and deeper DeFi (AI-routed swaps, perps, liquidity management). Quote from CEO Ivan Soto-Wright.

Launch x402 payees were AgentRes.dev (restaurant reservations), Purch.xyz (shopping) and BRIJ.fi (flights). Neeraj Prasad, MoonPay Labs chief engineer and Dawn Labs founder, promised more AI platforms and DeFi (swaps, perps, liquidity) within about a month. MoonPay also acquired Entendre and Dawn Labs.
PayBox's own API llms.txt says agents 'take positions on World prediction markets, and pay x402 services across the open internet (buy on Amazon with Solana USDC, book a table through Resy on Base)'.
Aug 27, 2026: 'PayBox has added Kamino as its first crypto lending and yield plugin.' Not available in the US, UK, EU or Australia.
Aug 31, 2026: PayBox went live in Grok as a custom connector (grok.com/connectors, server URL api.paybox.sh/mcp, OAuth). No mention of Grok Bots or a marketplace.
Jupiter went live inside PayBox on Sept 3, 2026, bringing routing, limit orders, DCA and earn products to Claude, ChatGPT and Grok.
MoonPay's September recap on X lists 'added Grok to PayBox', 'added Jupiter to PayBox' and 'added Sunrise to PayBox' (post decodes to Oct 1, 2026). Seen only via a search snippet.

The public PayBox app JS bundle has a pluginLogo map with slugs xp, collector-crypt, aave, world, hyperliquid, jupiter, sunrise, whop, kamino and maple, plus a separate 'dflow' partner icon next to 'world'. Reading these as official plugin slugs is an inference.

The app's approval UI defines these operation types: payment, wallet_sign, secret, swap, transfer, prediction_trade (market_mint, side, size, slippage_bps), ticket_purchase (event_title, section/row, quantity, price in USDC, pay_to; network fees from the Solana wallet), commerce_purchase (merchant, item_title, quote, delivery_email, settle destination) and undelegate_account. There is also an OAuth-connected 'xp' plugin connection (/api/plugins/xp/oauth/start).

Unofficial plugins are served from /api/open-plugins/* (catalog, connections, sandbox releases). A plugin's target kind is either 'remote' (an MCP URL, with optional OAuth start) or 'sandbox' (a hosted release with version_id). Before enabling a sandbox release, the user reviews 'Network access' (egress hosts plus brokered header hosts), 'Developer-provided credentials', 'Environment settings' and 'Tools'.

Developer guide: x402 'hosted payment endpoints must use a configured network host; remote plugins use their connected origin'. Submitted projects appear under 'Unofficial plugins' for private testing. Publication to other users requires manual approval of every version. Agents find installed plugins with discover_plugins/get_plugin and call them with use_plugin.

Agent routing rules: for provider jobs (Solana limit order, liquidity-pool investment, concert tickets), search both discover_plugins and discover_services. Include disabled official plugins (share their enable_url). Read an official plugin's contract_uri with get_contract. Unofficial plugins return their tool schemas directly in discovery.

World Prediction Markets is a non-custodial Solana protocol that routes orders to Solana liquidity providers. Each position is an SPL token, resolution uses Chainlink oracles and payouts redeem automatically. It replaced DFlow/Kalshi as Phantom's prediction-market infrastructure from June 1, 2026. The team is anonymous; no token or funding has been disclosed.

World settles in CASH, Phantom's dollar stablecoin. It rolled out inside Phantom in July, and the standalone world.xyz launched with a 1M+ waitlist and went offline briefly from traffic. It keeps integrations with Phantom and MoonPay's PayBox.
PayBox docs: geofenced World money tools are MCP-only. When World is enabled, outcome balanceUsd comes from the held side's orderbook midpoint.

SDK 0.7.0 (published July 8, 2026) already shipped plugin tools world_* and hyperliquid_*, with CLI examples 'paybox world buy --mint <outcome-mint>' and 'paybox hyperliquid markets # spot discovery'. So both plugins predate the public launch.

@paybox-sh/sdk timeline: 0.1.0 on 2026-06-08 (published by npm user njdawn, nj@dawnlabs.ai); 0.8.0 on Aug 27; 0.8.5 on Aug 31 (adds Grok Bot/Grok Computer CLI path); 1.0.0 on Sept 17 (generic plugin discovery, Muse support, per-plugin CLI groups removed); 2.0.0 on Oct 2 (get_deposit_link); 2.2.0 on Oct 14 (runPlugin/resumeRequest). The README example selects plugin id 'aave'.

MoonX is a MoonPay platform, not a third party. The @moon-x/* npm packages are maintained by moonpay-engineering (UNLICENSED) and describe 'embedded wallets with passkey-protected MPC signing for Ethereum, Solana, Tron, and Bitcoin' with moon_sk_* server keys and ephemeral signers. moonx.com did not resolve in DNS during this research.
MoonPay acquired the Israeli MPC/TEE key-management firm Sodot for about $100M (reported all-stock) on April 29, 2026. Sodot supplies the infrastructure behind PayBox.

Muse is Meta's personal AI agent, announced Sept 8, 2026. It runs on a dedicated 'Muse Secure VM' with its own browser, is rolling out in the US on iOS, Android and muse.ai, and uses Stripe Link one-time cards for purchases. Meta does not mention MoonPay.

The SKILL.md shipped in the PayBox SDK has a host capability table: Muse (link_surface phone_browser, no buttons, does not keep a process), Grok Bot (opens links in the app, renders buttons, keeps a process, no group login). grok.com uses the MCP connector, not the CLI.

Grok Bot is xAI's computer-use agent: durable bots with skills, sharing and a bot Marketplace, running on a shared persistent cloud computer. A third-party guide says it launched in August 2026 for SuperGrok Heavy and Cursor Ultra subscribers.

moonpay/paybox-plugin (MIT, created Aug 26, 2026) packages PayBox as a .grok-plugin with 3 skills, and its core tools include request_transfer. PR #413 'feat(plugins): add PayBox' to xai-org/plugin-marketplace has been open since Aug 28 and PayBox is absent from its marketplace.json (35 plugins). A Sept 18 commit says 'Cursor approved the PayBox plugin'.

PayBox is a product of Launchpad Limited, which MoonPay describes as an unregulated MoonPay group entity that never holds user funds. The hackathon sponsor is Launchpad Limited, a BVI company. Judging Panel members are 'selected by Launchpad' and may be announced before or during judging.

Support articles say 'Payment cards are coming in a future release. For now, wallets and secrets are available' and 'Payment card support is coming in Phase 2'. Secrets are returned raw to granted agents. The support approval modes are Always approve, Approve above limit, and Autonomous within policy.
PayBox Desktop (Mac only at launch) bundles the PayBox CLI, Claude Code and Codex CLI, shares skills across both, and offers native automations (scheduled recurring agent tasks).

Hackathon Chapter 1 runs Oct 16, 8am to Oct 17, 8pm EDT, in-person plus virtual, theme 'Agents & PayBox', $20k USDC pool with an illustrative split. Benefits: hardware wallet, VIP access (no onboarding fees), GTM advisory. Winners and honorable mentions enter the PayBox Marketplace 'ahead of its public opening'. The page bills x402 as 'the fast lane into Chapter 1'.

The official hackathon page links only to docs, support, privacy and terms. It has no Discord, Telegram, office-hours, judges or venue details, and says 'Open to eligible participants worldwide'. The portal can require an eligibility badge where the PayBox email must match the MoonPay KYC email.
@PayBox posted 'the first PayBox Hackathon is live! build a plugin for our marketplace and compete for $20,000 USDC in prizes' (the post ID decodes to about 2026-10-16 13:50 UTC).
A MoonPay employee's LinkedIn lists a 'PayBox Hackathon' at MoonPay's NYC Headquarters among MoonPay College campus events. Seen only via a search snippet; exact venue unconfirmed.

paybox.sh positioning: 'Trade, buy, book, & pay, all in one chat'. Example jobs include a Carbone table booked over x402, a SFO-JFK flight ('new services every week'), merchant-scoped one-time virtual cards for reorders and weekly pantry restocks under a cap, pay-per-use research ('spend up to $5 on search and scraping'), gas top-ups on every chain, weekly 60/40 rebalancing, DCA, and 'put my idle USDC to work... compared and executed by your agent'. Also: 'Any model. Any chain. Any app and exchange.' Gemini appears in the hero, but the app has no Gemini setup steps.
The launch went viral through a USDC faucet campaign (rewards reported from $5 to $1,000; required linking an X account). MoonPay gained about 35k X followers within a day and paused the faucet.

MoonPay's wider agent narrative: MoonPay Agents (Feb 2026) and the MIT-licensed Open Wallet Standard (Mar 23, 2026), with partners including PayPal, Circle, Solana Foundation, Ethereum Foundation, Base, DFlow, Allium and Virtuals, and an 'open skills marketplace'.

MoonPay's separate CLI skills ecosystem features x402 and data partners: Messari x402, Corbits paid-API marketplace, Myriad (BNB prediction markets), Zerion wallet data via x402, plus Maiat token safety, ThoughtProof, Shipp sports data, Dune and Allium. These are likely candidates for PayBox listings and possible overlap.

@paybox-sh/connect-react 0.1.1 (published Sept 17, 2026) provides 'Customizable Claude and ChatGPT connect buttons with built-in PayBox setup guides'. MoonPay wants third-party apps to onboard users into PayBox.

opportunities.title: Solana Pay and merchant invoice checkout plugin (Merchant tools)
opportunities.description: Tools: parse_payment_request(url or invoice id) returns a structured quote (merchant, amount, token, memo, reference). pay_invoice returns ONE unsigned legacy Solana transaction: a USDC TransferChecked with a createAssociatedTokenAccountIdempotent for the payee, the Solana Pay reference key and a memo, with the user's wallet as single signer and fee payer. verify_payment(reference) reads a configured RPC host and returns a receipt. An optional x402 variant covers merchants that expose x402 invoice endpoints.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: No merchant-side plugin is visible in the catalog. It fits MoonPay Commerce's Solana Pay heritage (MoonPay Commerce was formerly Helio; that link is my inference), suits the 'transact with a business' track wording, and demos cleanly end to end on mainnet with cents. A receipt and verification step scores on completeness.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: Fits the rules: one Solana transaction, a single signer and under 1232 bytes, and PayBox replaces the blockhash. Stateless: the reference is carried by the agent. The RPC host is one of the 16 allowed hosts, and its key can be a brokered header. Solana Pay transaction requests where the merchant co-signs do not fit the single-signer rule, so support transfer-request URLs and invoice APIs only.

opportunities.title: Pay-per-render creative studio over x402 (Creative)
opportunities.description: The builder hosts or wraps a generative endpoint (image, short video, voiceover, music stem or meme) behind x402 on Base USDC. The plugin's commission tool returns an x402 proposal (POST of 64 KiB or less, a maxAmount quote, expiry within 5 minutes). Free tools quote the price before paying and later fetch the result by job id, returning URLs and metadata as structured content.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: The Creative track has no first-party coverage at all. It uses MoonPay's pitch that x402 is 'the fast lane' and lets an agent 'commission and pay for directly'. Visual output makes the required X demo video compelling.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: The paid response comes back through the PayBox request, not the sandbox. Long renders therefore need an asynchronous design: pay, receive a job_id, then poll with a free status call. No custom headers are allowed on x402 calls, so authorization must ride on the payment itself. The endpoint host must be configured. Keep the price small so approval is easy in the demo.

opportunities.title: Forecast desk: fair-odds pricer and position sizer next to World (Predictions)
opportunities.description: Read-only tools pull public odds and data from Kalshi, Polymarket and sports or economic sources (some via paid x402 data). They return fair probabilities, the edge against World's book where data is reachable, Kelly-capped sizing, and a resolution-date and settlement checklist. The agent then executes with the first-party World plugin. An optional paid premium-signal tool settles through x402.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: It covers the 'price' and 'settle' parts of the Predictions track without duplicating World. It mirrors MoonPay's own interest (moonpay-scout arbitrage, Shipp sports data plus prediction-market skills) and shows composition across plugins, which the docs encourage.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: Pure data tools fit the 10-second budget and the 16-host limit. A plugin cannot call another plugin, so execution is left to the agent and World. Handle geofencing: World money tools are geofenced, and judges score compliance. Polymarket orders need EIP-712 signatures, so do not build trading there.

opportunities.title: Idle-cash sweeper and yield comparator with one-click deposit (Consumer finance)
opportunities.description: Compares live APYs and risk across Solana and Base venues (Kamino, Jupiter Lend, Maple and Aave read via public APIs, plus venues that have no official plugin). It returns ranked options and ONE deposit proposal for the chosen venue, preferring Solana single-transaction deposits or vaults where approval is not needed. It also adds a 'withdraw to cover bill X' helper.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: It directly realises the homepage promise 'Put my idle USDC to work... compared and executed by your agent'. Existing official plugins are each tied to one protocol, so a neutral comparator adds new value.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: An EVM ERC-20 deposit needs a separate approval proposal, so lead with Solana or native-asset paths. Respect geo-restrictions (Kamino is blocked in the US, UK, EU and Australia) and surface eligibility. Plugin money proposals always require approval, which is fine. Collision risk with the official Kamino, Jupiter, Aave and Maple plugins, so differentiate on comparison and on venues without a plugin.

opportunities.title: Pay-by-handle with safety screening (Consumer finance: moving money)
opportunities.description: Resolves an SNS .sol name, ENS, a Basename or an X-linked address to a wallet. It runs safety checks (address age, sanctions or scam lists through a paid API, a first-time-recipient warning) and returns ONE transfer proposal (Solana USDC or native ETH on Base) with a memo.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: An everyday money move with an obvious safety story that lines up with PayBox's 'agent never sees keys' trust narrative. It is easy to film for an X demo, for example 'send @friend $5'.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: Core already has a transfer tool (request_transfer in the plugin README), so the value must be resolution plus risk checks. Resolution APIs fit within 16 hosts, and API keys can be brokered headers. Stateless.

opportunities.title: Recurring-plan planner for gas top-ups, rebalancing and DCA (Consumer finance)
opportunities.description: Stateless planning tools take the user's holdings (passed in by the agent from get_portfolio) and a target policy such as 60/40, minimum gas per chain or a daily DCA amount. They return the next single action as a proposal or as a structured instruction for core request_swap. The host's scheduler (PayBox Desktop native automations, Grok Bot) re-invokes them each cycle.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: Three homepage scenarios (gas top-ups on every chain, 60/40 every Sunday, DCA) currently depend on the host. A plugin that makes them deterministic and auditable is distinctive.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: No persistent state or scheduler inside the plugin, so all state must travel with the agent. Only one transaction per call, and a plugin cannot invoke request_swap itself. It risks looking like glue unless it adds real logic such as thresholds, slippage caps and a dry-run report.

avoid: Rebuilding first-party coverage: Jupiter swaps, limit orders and DCA; Kamino lending; World prediction trading; Hyperliquid spot/perps; Aave and Maple yield. Judges will see this as low creativity, and the agent routing rules favour official plugins.
Duplicating core PayBox tools (request_swap, bridging, get_portfolio, get_buy_link on-ramp, a generic pay_x402/use_service wrapper, transfers). The plugin adds nothing the agent cannot already do.
Restaurant booking, Amazon-style shopping or flight-booking clones. AgentRes/Resy, Purch and BRIJ already serve these over x402 through discover_services.
Concert ticketing and collectibles purchases. The app bundle already models ticket_purchase and has xp and collector-crypt plugin logos, so collision is likely.
Anything that needs persistent state, timers or background jobs inside the plugin (price alerts, stop-losses, DCA bots). Every call gets a fresh sandbox with a 10-second budget.
Card-based checkout. Plugins can only propose EVM, Solana or x402 payments, and support articles say cards are 'Phase 2' or a future release.
Flows that need EIP-712, Permit2 or gasless signed orders (Polymarket CLOB, UniswapX, Jupiter Ultra). Hosted plugins cannot request EIP-712 signatures.

Using the end user's own exchange or API credentials (Coinbase or Kraken keys). Brokered headers are developer-provided and the plugin cannot read user secrets, so this fails compliance and feasibility.
Multi-step EVM ERC-20 flows (approve then action) as the demo centrepiece. Each step is a separate approval and the demo becomes clunky.
Geofenced financial products demoed without region handling. Prediction markets and Kamino-style lending are restricted in some jurisdictions, and 'compliance' is a judging factor.
Mostly AI-generated submissions or anything resembling credential misuse. The terms explicitly allow disqualification for both.
constraints_risks: The official plugin catalog cannot be read without authentication (api.paybox.sh/api/plugins and /api/open-plugins/catalog return 401). The plugin list here is inferred from public app-bundle logos, press releases and docs, so confirm it with discover_plugins from a logged-in agent before choosing an idea.

The marketplace has not opened to the public. Winners and honorable mentions enter it 'ahead of its public opening', and publication needs manual approval per version. Judges will likely test the plugin privately as an unofficial plugin.
No judges, Discord, Telegram or office hours are published. The terms say the panel may be announced during judging. The tie-breaker is at the panel's discretion.
Submission may be blocked until MoonPay KYC is done under the same email as the PayBox account. Complete it immediately.
The window is about 36 hours (Oct 16 8am to Oct 17 8pm EDT). After the deadline no further uploads are possible, though network hosts, variables and secrets can still be edited.
Geofencing: World money tools are geofenced and MCP-only, and Kamino is unavailable in the US, UK, EU and Australia. A builder's own region can block live demos of related flows.

There are no formal xAI, Anthropic or OpenAI partnership statements. Claude, ChatGPT and Grok all use custom connectors, and the xAI marketplace PR #413 is unmerged. Do not claim partnerships in the demo.
Launchpad Limited (BVI) is described as unregulated. Avoid regulated-product framing and any wording that implies MoonPay endorsement or uses MoonPay or PayBox branding as your own.
World's docs require login and its team is anonymous. Integrating World directly, rather than through the official plugin, is high-risk and unverified.
I could not finish the scan for other participants' public projects because the shared web-search budget ran out. GitHub API rate limits also blocked part of the repo checks.

Is 'sunrise' Wormhole's Sunrise asset gateway on Solana? Is 'whop' the source of commerce_purchase? Is 'xp' XP's Solana ticketing marketplace? These are inferred and unconfirmed.
Which chains count as 'PayBox-supported' for plugin EVM proposals? Are Tempo, Arc, Robinhood Chain and Hyperliquid EVM accepted for plugin calls, or only the core chains?
How will judges exercise submissions: by enabling them under Unofficial plugins in their own PayBox accounts, by watching the X demo only, or both? Is a minimum or maximum video length required?
Does World enforce US geofencing (likely, but not verified)? Does World expose a public trade API, or is it reachable only through PayBox's first-party plugin?

Will MoonPay announce judges or hold office hours during Oct 16-17 (for example on @PayBox or @moonpay on X)? Is there an in-person check-in at the NYC office that matters for virtual participants?

summary:
As of 16 Oct 2026, x402 is the main open standard for agents paying over HTTP. The Linux Foundation now runs it as the x402 Foundation (intent April 2026, operational 14 Jul 2026, 40 members). MoonPay is a Premier member alongside Coinbase, Cloudflare, Stripe, Visa, Mastercard, Google, AWS, Circle and Shopify. MoonPay's stated thesis, "the entire financial operation behind those payments is native to the agent", is a ready-made pitch for the judges.

x402 v2 (spec dated 2025-12-09) changes:
- The challenge moves into a base64 PAYMENT-REQUIRED header. PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and PAYMENT-RESPONSE replace X-PAYMENT and X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE.
- Networks use CAIP-2 IDs.
- A ResourceInfo block (serviceName, tags, iconUrl) is added.
- Extensions are added: bazaar, sign-in-with-x, payment-identifier, offer-and-receipt, builder-code and gas sponsoring.

Schemes are exact (EIP-3009 or Permit2), upto, batch-settlement (launched May 2026; includes Cloudflare's credit-backed cloudflare:402) and auth-capture (escrow, void, refund, reclaim on Base commerce-payments; spec v1.1, Aug 2026). No public facilitator supports auth-capture yet. The refund extension is unmerged, and the spec puts budgets and sessions explicitly out of scope.

Real usage is small and noisy:
- **x402scan:** about 2.96M transactions and $1.18M over 30 days; $105k in the last 24h, 88% of it through one facilitator (FluxA).
- **x402-list:** $419k over 30 days to listed services; 63% went to one service, almost all from a single buyer.
- **x402.org dashboard:** showed $24M for 30 days (as of 25 Aug), which conflicts with both explorers.

The CDP Bazaar lists about 40.8k endpoints on about 2.4k hosts (median price $0.01, 99% on Base). Only about 1.3% of listings have 10 or more unique payers. That is roughly 393 listings on 115 hosts, close to the pool PayBox's discover_services draws from. About a quarter of those look like sybil "sweep" traffic, and Bazaar counters may count payments that were verified but never settled. Demand clusters in:
- LLM routing (BlockRun)
- search and enrichment (Exa via StableEnrich, Tavily, You.com)
- X/Twitter data
- plain chain reads (OneSource)
- crypto intelligence (Nansen, Arkham)

Commerce (Bitrefill, StableTravel) and creative generation are thin.

Competing protocols are converging with x402 rather than replacing it:
- **MPP (Stripe + Tempo):** IETF draft with charge, session and subscription intents. 127 of its 130 curated services pay on Tempo. The mppx SDK lets one server accept both MPP and x402.
- **Stripe:** settles MPP and x402-on-Base payments into a Stripe balance.
- **Card checkout:** ACP (OpenAI + Stripe, beta) and UCP (Google + Shopify, with AP2 mandates) handle card checkout. Visa Intelligent Commerce Connect and Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines (partners include MoonPay and Basis Theory) tokenize cards for agents.
- **Agent wallets:** Coinbase Agentic Wallets, Circle Agent Stack, FluxA, Crossmint, AWS AgentCore payments and MoonPay's own MoonAgents all add spending limits on top.

PayBox's niche is the approval, policy and audit layer the user owns, across cards, wallets and secrets.

The PayBox plugin rules shape what can be built:
- payments are exact amounts in USDC on Base or Solana only
- proposals expire within 5 minutes
- no custom headers
- at most 16 configured hosts, so a universal router or bridge is impossible
- every payment tool needs the user's approval
- the plugin is not resumed after payment; a second call is needed to use the paid result

Designs that fit:
1. Do the work on your own server, so one approval buys one checked result.
2. Fill the gaps x402 leaves on the money side: escrow and refunds on Base AuthCaptureEscrow, signed offers and receipts, spend ledgers.
3. Avoid saturated $0.01 data wrappers, subscriptions, multi-payment pipelines and inflating unique-payer counts.

key_facts.fact: The x402 repo moved to the x402 Foundation org (github.com/x402-foundation/x402, ~6.7k stars, active 2026-10-15); coinbase/x402 is now described as a 'development fork'.

x402 v2 spec (v2.0 dated 2025-12-09; launch blog Dec 11, 2025): CAIP-2 network IDs; PaymentRequired carried as base64 PAYMENT-REQUIRED response header; client sends PAYMENT-SIGNATURE; server returns PAYMENT-RESPONSE (replacing X-PAYMENT/X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE); separate ResourceInfo block {url, description, mimeType, serviceName<=32 ASCII, tags<=5, iconUrl}; extensions map of {info, schema} that clients must echo.

v2 defines payment flows: 'authorization' (default: verify -> run handler -> settle, so a failing handler is not charged), 'upfront' (settle first) and 'escrow' (settle deposit -> resource -> settle final); adds a non-terminal 'settlement_pending' error that must carry the broadcast tx hash.
The x402 v2 spec explicitly lists 'Client-side budget management' and 'Session handling mechanisms' as out of scope.

Scheme specs in the Foundation repo: exact (EVM via EIP-3009 or Permit2; bindings also for SVM, Stellar, XRPL, TON, NEAR, Sui, Aptos, Algorand, Cardano, Hedera, Starknet, Canton, Concordium, Keeta, Casper, Lightning 'lnbtc'), upto, batch-settlement (EVM, SVM, and a Cloudflare binding), auth-capture (generic + EVM).
upto = single-use, time-bound authorization of a maximum amount; settled amount <= max (may be 0); explicitly does NOT cover streaming/multi-settlement, recurring payments or open-ended allowances.

batch-settlement: client commits (escrow/channel 'capital-backed' or identity/billing 'credit-backed'), access is granted immediately, value is redeemed later in bulk; supports dynamic pricing up to a per-request ceiling. Cloudflare's 'cloudflare:402' binding is credit-backed, authenticated with RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures, with Cloudflare as merchant of record (pay-per-crawl style).
x402 batch settlement was announced May 11, 2026 by Cloudflare and Coinbase engineers; TypeScript and Go SDKs support it, Python in development.

auth-capture scheme (v1.0 2026-05-13, v1.1 2026-08-18): authorize/charge/capture/void/refund plus payer-only 'reclaim' after the capture deadline; default flow is escrow; EVM binding uses base/commerce-payments AuthCaptureEscrow with ERC3009/Permit2 collectors and operator types 'delegated'/'custom' ('policy' reserved).

- amount: maxAmount in atomic units
- expiry: within 5 minutes
- requests: HTTPS on port 443; GET with no body or POST with at most 64 KiB JSON
- no custom headers or credential injection; endpoint must be a configured host
- PayBox fetches the live 402 and verifies asset and amount
- dev validation sends the unpaid request, which can trigger provider side effects
- the paid response comes back through the PayBox request; the plugin is not resumed

opportunities.title: EscrowPay: buyer-protected agent checkout on Base (x402 auth-capture semantics via AuthCaptureEscrow)
opportunities.description:
A Merchant-tools / Consumer-finance plugin plus a small operator service the builder hosts. Tools:
- quote_protected_purchase: returns a PaymentInfo with amount cap, captureDeadline, refundDeadline and fee bounds for a merchant SKU or service.
- fund_escrow: two EVM proposals, a USDC approve to PreApprovalPaymentCollector and preApprove(paymentInfo). Alternative: return ERC-3009 typed data the agent signs with core request_wallet_sign, then a second call relays it.
- escrow_status: reads AuthCaptureEscrow state from chain.
- confirm_delivery / dispute: calls the operator API to capture or void.
- reclaim: EVM proposal calling reclaim after the capture deadline.
Demo: the merchant fails to deliver, funds come back; or the merchant delivers, capture fires and a signed receipt is issued.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: Refunds and escrow are x402's most cited unsolved gap. The auth-capture spec (v1.1, Aug 2026) has no public facilitator support, the refund extension is unmerged, and an audit found about 4.5% of spend wasted on useless responses. It maps directly to MoonPay's stated thesis ('the entire financial operation behind those payments'). PayBox passkey approvals plus the audit trail make it consumer-grade buyer protection. It uses audited contracts, spans two tracks, and gives a clear before/after story for the video.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: Base is a PayBox chain. Each proposal is one call, with the ERC-20 approve as a separate proposal, so 2 approvals. The plugin cannot request EIP-712 signatures, so use the PreApproval collector or ask the agent to call request_wallet_sign. The operator key must live in the builder's external service (one of the 16 hosts; protect the operator API with a brokered header). State lives on chain, so no sandbox memory is needed, and on-chain reads fit in 10s. Risks: correct PaymentInfo encoding/hash, operator gas, deadline handling. Test with small amounts on mainnet before Saturday 8pm New York time.

opportunities.title: Outcome-guaranteed x402 service: one approval buys one verified result
opportunities.description:
Ship the product as an x402 v2 endpoint that uses the default 'authorization' flow: verify payment, run the work (aggregating several upstream APIs on the builder's server with the builder's keys), validate the output against a published contract, and settle only if it passes. Return a signed offer and receipt (offer-and-receipt extension) and machine-checkable evidence. The PayBox plugin exposes typed zod tools:
- quote: free; shows price, what is guaranteed, and an example
- buy: x402 proposal with maxAmount
- verify_receipt: run on the paid response the agent passes back
opportunities.why_it_could_win: Market analyses agree the bottleneck is buyer confidence and the second call, not payment rails. Zero of about 40.8k Bazaar listings publish an output schema, and failed first calls kill retention. PayBox requires approval for every payment, so 'one approval = one guaranteed outcome' is the best possible UX. Judges score completeness, usefulness and technical execution.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: Exact USDC on Base or Solana. The plugin only builds the proposal envelope (well under 10s); heavy work runs on the builder's server. No custom headers, so carry parameters in the query string or a POST JSON body (64 KiB max). Make the unpaid 402 path free of side effects, because dev validation sends unpaid requests. Processing the paid response needs a second plugin call. Open question: PayBox's timeout when it fetches the paid resource.

opportunities.title: Curated vertical router with x402 pre-flight safety checks (up to 16 providers)
opportunities.description:
Pick one non-LLM vertical, such as research/search, B2B enrichment or travel. A plan tool:
- probes live 402s from a curated provider set in parallel (e.g., Exa direct, StableEnrich, Tavily, You.com, Firecrawl)
- validates each challenge: v1/v2 sanity, Base/Solana USDC, payTo and price versus listing and category median, uptime and compliance grade from the x402-list API
- returns one x402 proposal to the best-value provider, with a plain-language pre-approval summary
A normalize tool turns the paid response the agent passes back into a common schema with citations and a receipt.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: It directly fixes documented failure modes: payee and price drift, broken examples, mixed v1/v2 challenges, settlement headers the chain doesn't confirm. It exploits real price spread (search from $0.005 to $0.025). It goes beyond PayBox's discover_services, which only filters on 10+ payers. It makes PayBox's raw transaction window meaningful.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: The 16-host limit caps providers plus metadata APIs, so this must be a curated set, not a universal router. Parallel unpaid probes have to fit within 10s. Providers that need API keys or custom headers cannot be paid through plugin proposals. A two-call pattern (propose, then normalize) is mandatory. Avoid LLM routing, which is crowded (BlockRun, JarvisClaw, Losbeto).

opportunities.title: x402 Ledger: chain-derived spend statements, receipts and anomaly alerts
opportunities.description:
A read-only Consumer-finance plugin. Given the user's wallet address(es), it reconstructs x402 spend from Base USDC TransferWithAuthorization events and Solana USDC transfers, and labels counterparties with Bazaar and x402-list metadata. It outputs:
- monthly statements by service and category
- flags for duplicate charges, price spikes against category medians, and payTo mismatches
- verification of offer and receipt signatures where present
- CSV/JSON export for expense or tax use
It can also suggest grant or budget settings in plain language.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: x402 explicitly leaves budget management out of scope, and the Foundation has a Tax working group. It needs zero approvals, so the demo is very reliable. It fits Consumer finance and MoonPay's 'financial operation' framing. It adds merchant-level meaning that PayBox's audit events and other agent wallets (FluxA, Coinbase) only partly provide.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: Needs indexer APIs (e.g., Basescan/Etherscan v2, Alchemy, Helius), with keys as brokered headers, within the 16 hosts. Page by time window to stay under 10s. Stateless. It cannot read PayBox's internal audit log, only on-chain data. Mapping payTo to a service is imperfect (Stripe's dynamic deposit addresses, facilitators). Pair it with one money action to show depth, e.g., a top-up suggestion through core get_buy_link.

opportunities.title: Creative commissions with signed license receipts (Creative track)
opportunities.description: An x402-paid generative service (image, short video, music or voice; the builder's server calls upstream models with its own keys). The paid POST returns a job ID plus a JWS license and receipt (offer-and-receipt) that binds the prompt hash, output hash, price and usage rights. A free get_result tool fetches the asset in a later call, each call under 10s. Optional: a provenance check that verifies the receipt against the delivered file.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: The Creative track brief is literally 'commission and pay directly'. Creative supply on x402 is thin compared with data wrappers. A signed license makes outputs usable commercially and is new in x402-land. MoonPay already sponsors an AI film festival with Venice, an x402 seller. It makes a very demo-able X video.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: Generation takes longer than 10s, so use an async job pattern: the paid call returns fast, and later free plugin calls carry the job ID the agent passes back, so no sandbox memory is needed. Exact USDC on Base or Solana. The unpaid 402 probe must not start jobs. Keep the request JSON at 64 KiB or less (send prompt text, not uploads).

opportunities.title: Agent-payable business invoices over x402 (Merchant tools)
opportunities.description: Merchants issue invoices as unique HTTPS URLs whose 402 challenge is bound to the invoice amount, payTo and expiry. The paying agent uses the plugin's pay_invoice tool (an x402 proposal) and gets a signed receipt. The server rejects duplicate payment of the same invoice before settling. Merchant-side tools create, list and check invoice status and export reconciliation records. Optionally the server also accepts MPP (via mppx) and settles into Stripe (x402 on Base via a Stripe deposit address) for fiat reconciliation.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: It matches the Merchant tools brief ('payment flows that let an agent transact with a business'). x402 has no invoicing semantics. The approve-then-pay flow mirrors how businesses already approve invoices before paying (accounts-payable), using PayBox approvals and audit. It reuses the same rails PayBox already pays.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: One host (the builder's invoice API). Invoice state lives on the builder's server. Plugin proposals cannot add the payment-identifier extension or headers, so enforce idempotency by invoice ID in the URL. Proposals expire in 5 minutes, so the plugin must fetch a fresh challenge per payment. Stripe x402 requires US eligibility, excluding New York.

opportunities.title: Post-hackathon distribution: earn real unique payers to also appear in PayBox discover_services
opportunities.description:
Make the builder's endpoint discoverable:
- CDP facilitator plus the bazaar extension (declareDiscoveryExtension with input and output schema)
- serviceName, tags and iconUrl; an https resource.url (set 'trust proxy'); a description under 500 chars with a 'use when' sentence
- a cheap GET preview route at $0.001-0.005
- register on x402scan, x402-list, Agentic.Market and pay.sh
- serve MPP alongside x402 via mppx for MPPScan and mpp.dev listing; Stripe Directory if on Stripe
opportunities.why_it_could_win: Only about 1.3% of listings reach the 10+ payer bar PayBox curates on. No listing publishes an output schema, which CDP search reportedly rewards. GET routes convert about 2x better. The plugin, Bazaar listing and directories reinforce each other.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: Not required for judging: plugin x402 proposals can target any configured host without Bazaar traction. Never inflate payer counts with sybil wallets; 'sweep' patterns are already flagged publicly and it would breach compliance terms. Open question: whether PayBox echoes the bazaar extension in payloads it builds, which determines whether PayBox-originated payments count toward Bazaar.

avoid: Generic pay-per-call data wrappers (weather, token prices, chain reads/RPC, web search/scrape, X/Twitter data, crypto market data, token-risk scanners). About 40.8k Bazaar listings, median $0.01, 77% have 2 or fewer payers, and the $0.01 band has the weakest demand; judges will see them as commodity.

LLM gateways or model routers: dominated by BlockRun, JarvisClaw, Losbeto, FarOut, Gondola, Venice, x402engine and others. No differentiation, and per-call approvals make chatty inference painful in PayBox.

A standalone paid 'trust/reputation layer' for x402 services: already crowded (x402-list assessments, Strale, agents-trust.com, AIMarket, Tanod), and analysts observe 'Everyone is building the trust layer, and few agents are buying it'. Embed trust checks in a useful flow instead.

Inflating unique payers or Bazaar listings with sybil wallets or verify-only payloads to get into PayBox's curated set. Tanod already flags 'sweep' patterns and issue #3226 exposes the verify loophole; it also risks disqualification under compliance terms.

Subscriptions or recurring billing through a plugin. Every plugin money tool needs user approval, there is no persistent sandbox state, and x402 has no subscription scheme (MPP does, but it is Tempo-centric).
Multi-payment pipelines (paying N services per user request inside the plugin). Each needs its own approval and follow-up plugin call; aggregate on your own server and charge once.

Designs that depend on upto, batch-settlement, sessions or streaming through PayBox. PayBox signs EIP-3009 exact only and plugin proposals are exact USDC on Base/Solana; upto (778) and batch (135) listings are tiny anyway.
'Universal' bridges or routers to any x402, MPP or ACP endpoint. Plugins can only reach 16 exact hostnames, and x402 proposals must target configured hosts.

Bridging ACP/UCP/Stripe SPT checkout by passing card numbers through the plugin. This violates PayBox's model (it never exposes raw card data), raises PCI concerns, and breaches the 'must not misuse credentials' term; card checkout belongs to PayBox core request_payment.
MPP-only (Tempo) services or x402 services only on Arc, Robinhood Chain, Polygon or Monad as payment targets. Plugin x402 proposals support only Base/Solana USDC, and MPP push mode is optional.

Agent-to-agent price negotiation marketplaces. No protocol supports negotiation, and PayBox's per-payment human approval conflicts with autonomous haggling; it will read as vaporware in a 2-day build.

Pitching traction with headline x402 numbers (75M tx, $24M per 30 days, 200M cumulative). Explorers show about $1.2M per 30 days and heavy concentration and wash activity; informed judges will discount it.
Relying on the x402.org facilitator for mainnet (testnet-only) or on Bazaar indexing for the demo. Indexing can lag, silently skips http:// resource URLs, and needs a settled payment.
constraints_risks:
PayBox plugin x402 proposals:
- exact USDC only, on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana mainnet
- maxAmount in atomic units; expiry within 5 minutes
- HTTPS on port 443; GET with no body or POST with at most 64 KiB JSON
- no custom headers or credential injection, so services needing API keys, sign-in-with-x or extra auth cannot be paid through plugins
Plugin x402 payment targets must be configured hosts, and the total network allowlist is at most 16 exact hostnames. Any router, aggregator or bridge is therefore capped and must be curated.
x402 via a plugin is two-step: the sandbox ends before approval. The agent polls get_request for the paid response and must call the plugin again to post-process. Design every flow around that.

Every plugin money tool requires user approval, even under autonomous grants. The PayBox transaction window shows raw details only, so plain-language summaries must come from tool output the agent relays.
x402 requires a plain EOA payer. EIP-7702-delegated PayBox wallets need an undelegate step (a composite flow where enabled), which can trip up demos. Pre-test the exact wallet.
Developer validation sends the unpaid request to your endpoint. The 402 path must have no side effects (no job creation, no inventory holds).
The 10-second budget per call covers probing live 402s, on-chain reads and indexer queries. Parallelize and paginate; use async job IDs for slow work.
There is no persistent sandbox state. Durable state (orders, invoices, escrow) must live on chain or in the builder's own service.

Spec instability: the offer-and-receipt wire shape is 'not stable', auth-capture is a v1.1 draft with no facilitator support, and the refund extension is unmerged. Pin SDK versions (@x402/* 2.28.0) and keep implementations self-contained.

x402 metrics are noisy and inconsistent across sources (x402.org vs x402scan vs x402-list). Bazaar counters may include verify-only or sybil traffic, which also affects PayBox's curated discover_services pool.

The CDP mainnet facilitator needs CDP API keys and applies KYT/OFAC checks. Stripe x402 and Cloudflare Monetization Gateway are US-only (Stripe excludes New York), so they may not suit a non-US builder.
Hackathon timing: upload plugin.mjs and submit before Saturday (Oct 17, 2026) 8pm New York time. Publication needs manual approval per version, and quota is 1 start per second and 1,000 per 24h.

Research limitation: the web-search budget ran out mid-task, and docs.cdp.coinbase.com and coinbase.com were unreachable from this environment. CDP Bazaar ranking details and Agentic Wallet limits therefore come from secondary sources (medium confidence).
open_questions: Does PayBox's plugin x402 path pass extension data (bazaar, offer-and-receipt, payment-identifier) through into the PaymentPayload it builds, and does it return the PAYMENT-RESPONSE settlement and receipt extensions to the agent? This decides whether PayBox-originated payments count toward Bazaar listing and whether signed receipts reach the user.
Does PayBox accept only EIP-3009 exact challenges, or also Permit2/upto, Solana upto (payment-channels) or batch-settlement? pay_x402 docs mention EIP-3009 only.

Which EVM chains count as 'PayBox-supported' for EVM proposals? Specifically: Tempo (eip155:4217), Arc (5042) and Robinhood Chain (4663). That decides whether any MPP push-mode bridge or Arc/Robinhood x402 targets are feasible.

How exactly does PayBox compute '10+ unique payers in 30 days'? Directly from the CDP Bazaar quality block (l30DaysUniquePayers), from its own settlement data, or including PayAI or other catalogs? And does it exclude sweep or verify-only traffic?

What timeout and retry behavior does PayBox apply when it fetches the paid resource after approval? This matters for server-side aggregation and outcome validation. How does it handle a 'settlement_pending' response?
Does the hosted plugin's 16-host allowlist allow redirects (e.g., CDN-hosted assets) for x402 targets and data fetches?
Will judges weight live mainnet USDC transactions over testnet? Is there any PayBox-provided test funding for demos?
Will any facilitator (CDP, PayAI, Dexter) ship auth-capture or the refund extension soon? That could either simplify or commoditize an escrow/refund plugin.
Cloudflare Monetization Gateway's closed beta lists 'eligible U.S.-based sellers and buyers'. Can arbitrary x402 wallets (e.g., PayBox users outside the US) pay Gateway-protected domains?

Does MoonPay plan PayBox support for card-network agentic tokens (Mastercard AP4M, where MoonPay and Basis Theory are partners; Visa Intelligent Commerce)? If so, which plugin-level hooks would exist for merchant (ACP/UCP) checkout?

summary: FACTS. As of October 2026, MoonPay has more than 35M customers and 1,500 enterprise clients, and it runs two stacks. The first is regulated payments and stablecoin infrastructure. It includes ramps (Headless Onramps from May 2026, Guest/Express Checkout from September 2026) and MoonPay Commerce (formerly Helio, 6,000+ merchants). It also includes MoonPay Enterprise (formerly Iron: pay-in, convert, pay-out, issue), Deposits (Glide), Trade (Decent) and Institutional (Sodot, led by Caroline Pham), plus the pending North Capital deal for tokenized securities. On stablecoins it has M0, PYUSDx with PayPal, Exodus USD and a Korea/KRW effort. Licences: BitLicense, NY trust charter, MiCA and a Dutch EMI. Partners: Mastercard, Visa, PayPal, Cash App. The second stack is an unregulated, non-custodial agent stack run by Launchpad Limited. Launchpad is the BVI subsidiary that runs this hackathon, and it also operates PayBox, MoonX WaaS, MoonPay CLI, MoonAgents and Dawn CLI. That stack shipped in order: MoonPay Agents/CLI (Feb), Open Wallet Standard (Mar), MoonAgents Card (May), the DFlow and Dawn acquisitions (May; Kalshi-on-Solana and AI prediction-market trading), MoonAgents Desktop (Jun), Entendre 'agentic finance' (Jun), PayBox (Jul 29), the Kamino plugin (Aug) and Grok (Aug 31). This hackathon is meant to fill the PayBox Marketplace. Ivan Soto-Wright called PayBox 'the product that MoonPay was built to make'. PayBox is a MoonPay Labs product (repo CODEOWNERS @moonpay/moonlabs). Its public voice is Neeraj Prasad, Chief Engineer of MoonPay Labs and founder of Dawn. He describes PayBox as 'your own money, on open rails', and says people will come 'because their AI can finally finish the job'. JUDGES. No judges are named; the terms say Launchpad picks them. The criteria have no weights: quality, completeness, compliance, creativity, usefulness, technical execution. INFERENCE (low-medium): the panel is probably MoonPay Labs/PayBox engineering and product (Prasad, Kevin Arifin), possibly with the GTM team and Ivan or Keith Grossman. Their written quality bar is the MoonPay skills rubric. Fake or unverifiable features are rejected outright. Tool descriptions must say exactly when to use them. Builders should point to core tools rather than copy them and must give clear security warnings. Their stated preference: '10 excellent' over '100 mediocre'. BEST MOONPAY INTEGRATION. MoonPay Commerce has an official x402 'agent-payable' checkout: POST to api.hel.io/v1/x402/checkout/{paylinkId}?payerAddress=... with USDC on Base or Solana, which are exactly PayBox's x402 rails. Commerce docs say every existing merchant is 'already agent-payable', and they list an MCP server and ACP as roadmap. A PayBox plugin that lets agents inspect, pay and verify Commerce paylinks and charges, and optionally lets merchants issue invoices, would: join two MoonPay business units; fit the Merchant tools track and the hackathon's 'x402 fast lane'; and arrive while MoonPay is pitching Commerce to merchants leaving Coinbase Commerce. Other options: Venice x402 credits for a Creative plugin (Venice co-presents MoonPay's Lumara AI Film Festival; awards Oct 26), DFlow/Kalshi for Predictions (without copying the first-party World plugin), and PYUSD or get_buy_link/Guest Checkout to cover funding shortfalls. WHAT GETS FEATURED (inference): a real mainnet, end-to-end demo of 60-90 seconds on a phone, in Claude, ChatGPT or Grok, in MoonPay's 'prompt, approve, pay' style. It should: need one or two approvals; show the cost before paying; work with core tools and lead into MoonPay revenue (ramps, swaps, Commerce volume); visibly respect compliance (no custody or secrets, aware of geofences); expose a small, clear set of tools; and show the builder's own design decisions, because work that is only AI-generated can be disqualified. AVOID: copycat x402 data wrappers, copies of core tools, plain Polymarket/Kalshi/Hyperliquid/Kamino trading, and booking or shopping clones of the launch partners.

opportunities.title: MoonPay Commerce Agent Checkout: inspect, pay and verify Helio paylinks and charges via x402 inside PayBox
opportunities.description: A small set of tools. (a) inspect_commerce_payment(url_or_id): GET api.hel.io/v1/charge/{token} or /v1/paylink/{id}/public and return merchant, product, price, accepted chains, expiry and an already-paid guard. (b) pay_commerce_payment(url_or_id, payer_address, chain, amount?): return an io.paybox/transactionProposal of kind x402 that POSTs to https://api.hel.io/v1/x402/checkout/{paylinkId}?payerAddress=...(&amount=) on eip155:8453 or solana:mainnet. Use /v1/x402/checkout/charge/{token} for Solana charges and /v1/x402/deposit/{id} for top-ups. (c) verify_commerce_payment: re-read the charge or paylink and return settlement status and tx hash. Optional merchant half: create_invoice (POST /v1/charge/api-key or /v1/paylink/create/api-key with a brokered merchant key). The demo can then show a merchant agent sending an invoice and a customer agent paying it, both on MoonPay rails.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: It joins two MoonPay business units (PayBox/MoonPay Labs and MoonPay Commerce, with 6,000+ merchants) using MoonPay's own documented agent-payment path. Commerce docs say merchants are 'already agent-payable' and list an MCP server and ACP as roadmap, so the plugin delivers that roadmap item inside PayBox. It sits squarely in the Merchant tools track and the hackathon page's 'x402 fast lane'. It completes real purchases ('finish the job') instead of fetching data. It supports Commerce's pitch to merchants leaving Coinbase Commerce, and the MoonPay GTM team (a winner perk) can turn it into a merchant story.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: Fits the plugin rules: an x402 proposal with exact USDC on Base or Solana, POST with no body, and payerAddress as a public query parameter (no custom headers or secrets). The agent supplies the payer's public address from the granted wallet list. It is stateless because the charge token or paylink ID is the handle. Host: api.hel.io. Test on day 1 with a $0.10-$1 dynamic paylink you create at moonpay.hel.io, and check: (1) PayBox handles Helio's x402 v2 headers; (2) the public paylink GET needs an Origin header, so confirm the sandbox allows it or use the charge GET instead; (3) paylinks with required customer fields return X402_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURES; (4) charge-resume is Solana-only; (5) the 10 requests/60 s per-payer-IP limit and the 30-120 s async sweep, so show a 'verified, settling' state.

opportunities.title: Agent invoicing and reconciliation for small merchants (Commerce plus the Entendre thesis)
opportunities.description: A merchant-side plugin that: creates a dynamic charge or paylink per invoice; lists paid vs unpaid invoices through Commerce transaction endpoints; expires stale charges; and returns structured reconciliation (invoice -> tx hash -> amount/chain -> suggested journal entry). It pairs with the checkout plugin above so one agent invoices and another pays.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: It mirrors MoonPay's Entendre acquisition ('agentic finance' reconciliation and bookkeeping; Ivan: 'The next financial system will be coordinated by humans and agents') and supports the Commerce and Enterprise GTM story. It is useful to real businesses beyond crypto natives and is clearly a Merchant tools entry.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: Needs a MoonPay Commerce merchant account. API keys go in host-scoped brokered headers (Bearer secret); publicKey is a query parameter, so confirm it can be stored as a plugin variable. There is no persistent state, so it re-queries Commerce on every call. The plugin moves no money itself, which means fewer approvals but less of a wow moment unless it is combined with the checkout plugin.

opportunities.title: Creative studio paid from PayBox via Venice x402 credits (Lumara tie-in)
opportunities.description: Tools: quote_generation (Venice video/music quote endpoints); fund_credits (x402 proposal to POST https://api.venice.ai/api/v1/x402/top-up, USDC on Base/Solana, $5 minimum); prepare_siwx(address), which returns the exact SIWE message for the agent to sign with core request_wallet_sign; then queue and retrieve tools that call Venice with the SIWX header and return media URLs.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: Venice co-presents MoonPay's Lumara AI Film Festival: finalists were announced 16 Oct 2026 and awards are 26 Oct in NYC, including a 'Rekt Award' for finance/crypto satire. A 'commission a short film or score from chat and pay per job' demo therefore lands on MoonPay's current marketing moment. It matches the Creative track wording ('commission and pay for directly') and shows a plugin x402 proposal working with a core wallet signature.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: The top-up fits PayBox's x402 rails exactly. Generation needs the SIWX header on ordinary fetches (check that the sandbox allows custom request headers) and a wallet signature the plugin cannot request itself, so the agent must call request_wallet_sign. Video jobs take longer than 10 s, so queue the job and retrieve it in a later call with the job ID. Venice markets itself as uncensored, so add your own content-safety checks to score on compliance. The first run needs two approvals (top-up and signature).

opportunities.title: Prediction-market pricing and hedge planner on MoonPay-owned rails
opportunities.description: A forecasting-first plugin. Given a user's question, or a portfolio passed in by the agent from get_portfolio, it returns fair odds and edge across venues and maps exposures to hedging markets. It then either routes entry through the first-party World plugin or returns one unsigned Solana transaction built with DFlow (MoonPay-owned; tokenizes Kalshi markets on Solana). It also includes a settle/redeem helper.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: It builds on MoonPay's DFlow and Dawn acquisitions and on the Predictions track's 'price, enter, and settle'. It stands apart through pricing and hedging logic rather than raw order entry, which MoonPay already ships (World plugin, CLI prediction-market skill, moonpay-scout, Dawn CLI).
opportunities.feasibility_notes: A single-signer Solana transaction of up to 1,232 bytes, with PayBox replacing the blockhash, fits API-built transactions. However, access to DFlow's prediction-market API (keys, endpoints) and its eligibility rules are unverified. World money tools are geofenced and Kamino is blocked in the US/UK/EU/AU, so build in eligibility checks. This option has the highest risk of overlapping first-party features.

opportunities.title: Shortfall-aware payment step that routes users to MoonPay ramps
opportunities.description: Every money tool first checks the cost against the balance the agent passes in. If funds are short, it returns structured 'needs_funding' data (exact USDC shortfall, chain, suggested action) instead of failing. The agent then calls core get_buy_link (MoonPay on-ramp, default usdc_base) or request_swap and retries. This can be built into any of the plugins above.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: It makes MoonPay's main revenue lines (ramps, swaps) visible in every flow and turns a zero-balance first-time user into a buyer. Guest Checkout lets new US users buy up to $750/week with Apple Pay or Google Pay before full verification. It also follows the PayBox README's 'tell the cost before paying' guidance.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: A plugin cannot call core tools, so it returns a plan the agent carries out. It needs no state, is cheap to add, and demos well.

avoid: Generic x402 data-API wrappers (crypto prices, news, research via Messari, Allium, Zerion, Nansen-style feeds): PayBox already surfaces curated x402 Bazaar services through discover_services/use_service, MoonPay's skills repo already ships these partner skills, and the 'x402 fast lane' will make this the most common entry, so it scores low on creativity and usefulness.

Re-implementing core tools (swap, bridge, on-ramp, transfer, portfolio): they duplicate request_swap, get_buy_link and get_portfolio, and MoonPay Labs' rubric explicitly says to cross-reference existing capabilities rather than duplicate them.
Plain Polymarket/Kalshi order entry: the first-party World plugin, the MoonPay CLI prediction-market skill, moonpay-scout, Dawn CLI and DFlow already cover it.
Hyperliquid perps or Kamino lending wrappers: first-party Hyperliquid and Kamino plugins already exist, and Kamino is geofenced.
Restaurant, flight or generic shopping booking clones: the launch partners AgentRes.dev, BRIJ.fi and Purch.xyz already fill this, so a copy reads as me-too.

Memecoin sniping or high-frequency bots: every plugin money operation needs user approval even under autonomous grants, the 10 s budget kills latency strategies, and it clashes with the 'trust layer' brand.
Anything custodial, with pooled funds, asking for keys or seed phrases, or proxying user credentials: it breaks the non-custodial model and triggers the 'misuse credentials' disqualification clause.

Securities/RWA or gambling-like products without eligibility or geofence handling: Launchpad is an unregulated entity, and MoonPay routes RWAs through regulated units (North Capital is still pending). Compliance is an explicit judging factor.

Testnet-only, mocked or 'coming soon' demos: entries must be live plugins working end to end, Commerce x402 has no testnet, and MoonPay Labs treats fabricated functionality as 'worse than no skill at all'.
Leaderboard, airdrop-farming or volume-wash concepts: an estimated 25-30% of x402 transactions are leaderboard chasing, and judges reward real usefulness.
constraints_risks: Judges are not named and criteria have no weights (quality, completeness, compliance, creativity, usefulness, technical execution). Tracks are starting points only; every entry is judged the same way.
Winning does not guarantee a marketplace listing. Every code version needs manual approval, so submit early to appear under 'Unofficial plugins' and leave time for review.

summary:
Facts first. In agentic-payments hackathons from 2024 to 2026, the generic 'agent pays for X' demo almost never takes 1st place. The winners I could verify fall into five types:
(1) A new economic mechanism built on a payment primitive while that primitive is still new. Examples: MCPay and Latinum monetising MCP via x402 in 2025; payload.exchange and Pincer letting sponsors pay an agent's HTTP 402 bill; Amiko's payment-weighted ratings; Intelligence Cubed's model revenue shares.
(2) Tangible or spectacular demos where value visibly moves. Examples: PlaiPin's ESP32 chip paying on its own, Paybot robots, ETHastic LoRa-radio payments, World of Geneva (AI agents playing an MMORPG while humans watch), and Onda auto-paying the artist you are listening to.
(3) Plain but real vertical commerce with a named buyer. Dairy Price API x402 won the Coinbase/AWS track at Consensus Miami 2026, and x402 Shopify Commerce was called the 'most practical' Solana x402 winner.
(4) Trust and verification layers: ENShell, DIVE, NewsFacts, zkx402, SecretAgent, ethui.
(5) Prediction-market structure: Capitola, Synthesis, Senthos, LYNX, Parabola, JetLagged, Moltbet.
Persistence also pays. Unruggable won Cypherpunk on its 4th attempt. MCPay won at ETHGlobal Prague, then Coinbase, then Colosseum, then got funded.

Judging rubrics converge:
- ETHGlobal scores Technicality, Originality, Practicality, Usability and WOW.
- Sponsor tracks reward sponsor-tech centrality. SKALE's x402 event scored 'agentic depth', 'commerce realism' and 'polish/ship-ability'. MoonPay's own track at the Synthesis hackathon required use 'beyond a basic demo'.
- Colosseum is judged by VCs: the pitch narrative, validation and founder-market fit matter most.
- Newer x402 contests score verified on-chain usage: Algorand runs a usage leaderboard, and BSV required 1.5M transactions in a 24-hour window.
- PayBox's terms list quality, completeness, compliance, creativity, usefulness and technical execution.

The space is very crowded:
- 97–98% of Arc submissions at HackMoney and Cannes 2026 were agentic.
- One analysis of 8,200 ETHGlobal projects found AI-agent projects grew from about 1% to over 20% of submissions.
- x402's hello-world example is literally GET /weather.
- One ERC-8004 track drew 403 projects.
- MoonPay judges have already seen several DCA, treasury and policy-guard agents in their Synthesis tracks.

Inference: any PayBox plugin that duplicates PayBox core will read as redundant. That includes approval and spend-policy layers, swaps, on-ramps, x402 gateways and Hyperliquid trading.

Inferred scoring model for 1st place at PayBox:
- Gates: live end to end with real money, compliant, and clearly human-made.
- About 25% usefulness and marketplace fit.
- About 20% PayBox-native depth: a transaction proposal or x402 payment, plus clear structured output and the approval moment.
- About 20% a mechanism that is not a cliché.
- About 20% clarity and wow in the X demo.
- About 10% robustness.
- About 5% traction proof.
Among finalists, originality plus a visible real-world outcome usually decides 1st; polish alone is necessary but not decisive.

Demo video. Primary guidance from ETHGlobal, Colosseum, Devpost and Arc agrees:
- State the value in the first seconds.
- Show the real product, not marketing.
- Cut out waiting.
- Use your own narration; ETHGlobal bans text-to-speech voiceovers.
- Prove the transaction on a block explorer.
On X, uploads from non-Premium accounts are capped at 140 seconds. Inference: aim for 60–90 seconds, with captions burned into the video. Hook with the outcome plus the passkey approval, and end on the transaction hash and 'live in PayBox marketplace'.

October 2026 news gives a timely 'rogue agent' story: an OpenAI model spent from other people's wallets, Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent, and Jamie Dimon warned about rogue agents. Inference: 'agent acts, human approves with a passkey' should land well with viewers right now.

Limits: the shared web-search budget ran out mid-research. coinbase.com, skale.space, DoraHacks and Medium could not be fetched, so those facts rest on search snippets.

opportunities.title: Cross-venue prediction-market 'price → enter → settle' plugin
opportunities.description:
Planned tools:
- quote_event: normalise one question across the venues the plugin can reach and return price, fees, liquidity and resolution source as structured data.
- explain_edge: text the agent can relay to the user.
- enter_position: one unsigned transaction on a PayBox-supported chain, or an x402-paid order call.
- redeem: proposal to claim winnings.
- Optional: pay for resolution evidence via x402.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: It fits the Predictions track word for word (price, enter, settle). Prediction-market aggregators and structure plays repeatedly won or got funded in 2025–26: Capitola (Cypherpunk Consumer 1st, then Cohort 4), Synthesis (Cohort 4), Senthos/Bench/Mentioned (Frontier 2026), LYNX (NY 2026 finalist), DIVE (Cannes 2026 finalist) and Parabola (Miami 2026 1st). The demo would show a real price comparison and one passkey approval, then the position on an explorer.
opportunities.feasibility_notes:
Constraints:
- At most 16 exact venue hostnames.
- No state: pass market and quote IDs in each call.
- Fetch quotes in parallel with timeouts to stay inside the 10-second budget.
- One transaction per call; ERC-20 approvals are separate proposals.
- The venue must be on a PayBox-supported chain (unverified: Polygon for Polymarket).

Risks:
- Order books that need EIP-712 signed orders cannot be signed by the plugin itself; the agent must call core request_wallet_sign.
- Compliance and geofencing are critical; the first-party 'world' plugin is geofenced. Add jurisdiction gating text.
- Must not duplicate the first-party hyperliquid or world plugins.

opportunities.title: Pay-the-creator media licensing / commission plugin (Creative)
opportunities.description: The agent finds or commissions an asset (image, track, clip or paywalled article) and pays the human creator per use through an x402 proposal in USDC on Base or Solana. It returns a license and provenance receipt (creator, tx hash, terms), with an optional split to collaborators. Triggers can be contextual, like Onda (pay when you listen) or NanoCrawl (pay per page read).
opportunities.why_it_could_win: Onda and NanoCrawl won Arc tracks at Cannes 2026, and zkx402 (content provenance on x402) was a Buenos Aires finalist. It is an emotional story with real money going to a real person, and it reads instantly in a 60-second video. It matches the Creative track ('commission and pay for directly').
opportunities.feasibility_notes:
The x402 proposal type fits directly: USDC on Base or Solana, expiry of 5 minutes or less, GET or POST with JSON up to 64KiB, and no custom headers. You need a real x402 endpoint for at least one creator (stand up a tiny one, or partner).

The paid response comes back through PayBox, so any post-processing needs a second explicit plugin call. There is no storage, so receipts must reference on-chain transaction IDs or an external store. Avoid generic AI-image-for-a-fee wrappers.

opportunities.title: Real-merchant agent checkout & invoice settlement (Merchant tools)
opportunities.description: Wrap one real business (your own product, or a willing small merchant) with three tools: list_catalog/quote, create_checkout (an order ID plus a human-readable summary) and pay (a single USDC transfer or x402 checkout proposal). Return a receipt the merchant's backend recognises. For merchants that only take cards, the agent can switch to core request_payment and claim_payment_credentials to get a one-time merchant-bound card.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: SKALE's x402 judges scored 'commerce realism'. x402 Shopify Commerce was called the 'most practical' Solana x402 winner, and a niche real data API (dairy prices) won Coinbase/AWS at Consensus Miami 2026. Arc noted that teams demoing to real businesses stood out. PayBox's mission is literally 'get your product into the marketplace'.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: The quote ID carries state, so the plugin itself stays stateless. One ERC-20 transfer per proposal. The merchant API key goes in a host-scoped brokered header. The PayBox transaction window shows raw details only, so the plugin's text must spell out item, amount and recipient. Avoid merchants that ban agents (Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent).

opportunities.title: Split-and-settle group pot (Consumer finance)
opportunities.description: The agent turns a receipt or trip-expense list into per-person shares and issues a 'settle my share' transfer proposal to the payer's chosen recipient. It can optionally return conversion quotes, and top-ups use core get_buy_link. Everything stays 'within policy': each move gets one clear approval.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: Everyday money moves that people relate to have won. C.E.S.T.A (Arc winner at Cannes 2026: friends pool USDC, Claude manages a road trip, merchants are paid by virtual card) and Text-to-Chain (HackMoney 2026 winner) are examples. The passkey approval of 'your $23.40 share' is a natural climax for the video, and PayBox's audit trail doubles as the ledger.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: All inputs are carried in the call, so no state is needed, and it fits the 10-second budget easily. Every plugin money move requires approval, so script a single hero approval for the demo. With no custom UI, return a structured split table plus text. A Solana single-signer transfer is also feasible.

opportunities.title: Pay-per-use physical device (spectacle demo)
opportunities.description: Put an x402 gate on a real device: a smart plug, printer, claw machine, EV-charger session or locker. The plugin returns an x402 POST proposal to the device endpoint. After the passkey approval, the device physically acts on camera.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: Hardware and physical demos are repeatedly rewarded and memorable. PlaiPin won at Solana x402 and placed 3rd in the Cypherpunk Undefined track. Paybot (robots via x402) and LensMint (camera) were Buenos Aires finalists, and ETHastic (LoRa mesh payments) was an Arc winner. 'Money moves, the world moves' works with the sound off on X.
opportunities.feasibility_notes:
The device needs a public HTTPS x402 endpoint, which must be one of at most 16 allow-listed hosts. POST JSON up to 64KiB with expiry of 5 minutes or less.

Risks: hardware failure inside 36 hours, and weaker 'usefulness'. Pick a device with a believable paying use case, and avoid coffee or pizza clichés.

opportunities.title: Verified data purchase with evidence receipts (trust layer that pays)
opportunities.description: The agent buys a specific, high-value fact (commodity price, flight status, match result or filing) via x402. It receives a verifiable bundle (source hash, timestamp, payment tx ID) that can resolve a prediction-market position, back an expense or feed an audit. A second plugin call verifies the bundle.
opportunities.why_it_could_win: Verifiability is a 2026 winning theme. Examples: NewsFacts (Arc on-site 1st, verifiable data commerce), Dairy Price API (Miami 2026 1st), DIVE (Cannes 2026 finalist) and Dolphin Sense (BSV grand prize; articles cite tx IDs). It matches PayBox's 'every op is an audit event' ethos without duplicating PayBox's approval layer.
opportunities.feasibility_notes: Pay with an x402 proposal, then verify on a separate call: this suits the 'sandbox ends before payment' model. Stateless, with the data provider allow-listed. Keep it inside the 10-second budget. Pick a vertical with a real buyer (commodities, logistics, sports), not weather.

avoid: Pay-per-call weather, quote, joke or 'premium data' wrappers. The x402 README's hello-world is literally GET /weather, and PayBox already pays any x402 endpoint natively (pay_x402 / use_service), so a thin wrapper adds no plugin value.

'Agent buys coffee, pizza or an Amazon item, or books a flight'. Crossmint already publishes these demos, and Amazon actively blocked Meta's Muse agent in Sept 2026, so this is both no novelty and a compliance risk.

Generic AI trading bots, DCA agents, auto-rebalancers and yield optimizers. MoonPay's own Synthesis tracks already got several DCA and treasury agents. PayBox ships a first-party Hyperliquid plugin plus core request_swap and get_portfolio. Plugins cannot schedule, keep state or batch approve+swap, so these demos look fake or clunky.
Another agent wallet, spend-policy, guardrail or approval layer (the Mandate, PolicyPay, AgentPay archetypes). PayBox is that layer already (grants, passkeys, audit), so judges will see redundancy.
MCP/x402 payment middleware, routers, gateways or facilitators. These won in 2025 (Latinum, MCPay, RequestTap), but PayBox now speaks x402 natively, so inside PayBox they duplicate core.

ERC-8004 reputation marketplaces or 'agents hiring agents' A2A economies as the headline. One Synthesis track drew 403 projects, and 97–98% of Arc submissions in 2026 were agentic, so it is undifferentiated.
Cross-chain bridging or 'any token, any chain' as the hook. Arc called it a 'baseline expectation' (56% of HackMoney entries), and core request_swap already bridges.
Generic tipping bots or creator tip jars. They are common and only fresh with a novel trigger plus a real recipient; Onda used automatic music detection plus escrow for unclaimed artists.
'Chat with your wallet' or natural-language on-chain command bots. These were 2025-era finalists (e.g. AIMen) and are now a commodity in every agent host.
Read-only dashboards or analytics with no money moving. They do not exercise PayBox's payment primitives, and PayBox renders no custom UI.

Demo anti-patterns:
